checks.acceptance: Default clothes, appearance and baked textures are visible immediately after login without Edit Outfit

Protocol checks verify own wearable IDs, outfit links and all six wearable assets. Separate protocol checks now pass baked texture upload and exact retrieval by the other account
checks.linux: Both distinct avatars render default clothes automatically in both Windows Firestorm sessions against Linux, without Edit Outfit. Linux protocol checks also pass own wearable IDs, all six wearable assets and cross-account baked-texture upload/retrieval

checks.acceptance: Two distinct accounts stay connected, see each other, and have isolated account and inventory state
checks.windows: Both distinct Firestorm accounts are simultaneously connected and each renders both named, clothed avatars. Second Only Preview Folder was created through Preview Second's inventory UI and is absent from Preview First's inventory search; protocol parent-folder isolation also passes
checks.linux: Both Windows Firestorm sessions against Linux display both distinct named clothed avatars before and after restart. The copied object is visible only in its Second owner inventory and absent from First inventory search. Linux protocol checks also verify distinct account IDs and parent-folder isolation

checks.acceptance: Both Firestorm avatars move normally and observe each other's movement
checks.windows: Both avatars moved through Firestorm arrow-key controls with position changes and remote avatar movement observed in the other viewer using ubODE
checks.linux: Verified with Windows Firestorm against Linux ubODE: user-held forward movement takes Second from about (128,128) to (133,129), and backward movement takes First from about (127,128) to (117,128). First renders Second at its displaced position; Second faces the nearest avatar and renders First at its new distant position. Human-assisted held inputs; rounded viewer coordinates

checks.acceptance: Create, rez, select, move, rotate, resize and edit basic objects through Firestorm
checks.windows: Firestorm creates and selects a cube, renames it Preview Second Persistence Cube, sets width 1.25 m, Z position 22.5 m and Z rotation 45 degrees, and takes an inventory copy through Build > Object > Take Copy. User-assisted inventory drag rezzes a distinct new object, verified in the viewer and persisted scene. Isolated protocol take-copy test passes with Flotsam memory caching
checks.linux: Verified through Windows Firestorm against Linux: create/select/name cube, width 1.25 m, position Z 22.5 m, Z rotation 45 degrees, Take Copy, and human-assisted normal inventory drag-to-world. Linux persistence confirms a distinct rezzed UUID, retained original and inventory item, correct Second owner, and identical scale/quaternion. Both viewers render both objects

checks.acceptance: Clean stop/start restores region objects, inventory and avatar state without repair
checks.windows: Both Firestorm clients log out, server exits with STOPPED, and both log back in after restart. Three viewer-created objects retain UUIDs, names, owners and positions; the copied inventory item and Second Only Preview Folder reappear in the inventory UI; both avatars render clothed automatically. Isolated protocol check additionally verifies flushing an appearance update before its delayed save
checks.linux: Both real Firestorm clients log out; Linux Docker server exits with STOPPED and code 0. Same volume restarts, both accounts relogin clothed and mutually visible, and both render the restored edited cube. Exact UUID/name/owner/position/scale/quaternion, inventory copy, appearance records and region cache ID survive. Second inventory displays its saved item; First search returns no item. Last avatar positions remain saved. No startup map warning Final follow-up clean restart preserves both exact cube transforms, inventory and appearance; two-account protocol check receives both restored objects and mutual avatar updates. No additional GUI Firestorm run for that final follow-up.
